answer: A farm that controls the author cannot also supply the quorum, because each signer must be independent on the kernel graph and each risks its bond. Because the ferrous release is logged with every signature, the beacon audit publishes the quorum and a forged release is rejected on replay. The escrow releases only against a quorum of 6 signatures from independent verifiers, so no single key can unlock a payout early. That is 22 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
